title: James
notes: Study aids companion for NT reading

footnotes.text: James 1:27.

Some similar themes between the teachings of Jesus and James include enduring persecutions (seeMatthew 5:10–12;James 1:2–3, 12); becoming “perfect,” or spiritually mature (seeMatthew 5:48;James 1:4;2:22); asking God (seeMatthew 7:7–8;James 1:5); doing the will of God (seeMatthew 7:21–24;James 1:22); loving others (seeMatthew 5:43–44;7:12;James 2:8); knowing good and evil by their fruits (seeMatthew 7:16–20;James 3:11–12); being a peacemaker (seeMatthew 5:9;James 3:18); and not swearing at all (seeMatthew 5:34–37;James 5:12).

The Greek wordoneidizō, translated as “upbraideth” in the King James Bible, means to “rebuke, reprimand; reproach; insult.” The underlying idea is “speaking disparaging words against someone or something” (Longman and Strauss,The Baker Expository Dictionary of Biblical Words, page 650).
